rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named — draft honours strategy's per-module mood, or flattens/contradicts it
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a module's opening framing pulling the student into the wrong mood before the arc even starts, which no later beat can fully correct. Strategy line 368 states the spirit explicitly: 'M4 doesn't prepare, it tests' — the module is framed against preparation-mindset on purpose, because M4→M5 is a test→learn contrast arc (mood: curious readiness). The file's Big Idea (line 4) opens 'Prep your first long session. The session is how you find out what's missing.' — 'Prep' is the lead word, and it recurs as the exercise link text 'Prep the run, fill the gaps' (line 39), so it is not an isolated slip but the module's chosen vocabulary. The harm is present, not just theoretical: this file's own maintainer Meta block (Mood target, line 103) names the exact drift to watch for — 'mood drift toward compliance-feeling ("did I prepare the right way?")' — and 'Prep' as the very first word a student reads is the surface most likely to seed that reading. The second Big Idea sentence partially recovers ('the session is how you find out what's missing' gestures at testing, not perfecting), but it does not cancel the lead word's framing.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Lead the Big Idea (and the exercise link text) with the testing/discovery framing strategy states explicitly, not 'prep' — e.g. open on what the session reveals, hold 'prep' (if kept at all) to describing the mechanical walk-and-fill steps rather than the module's stated purpose.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: unease framed as 'you did something wrong' rather than 'you don't yet know.' Checked the file's unease-adjacent lines — prework line 16 ('this module's un-watched session may look like exactly what that essay warns against') and 'Bring to Module 5' (line 66, 'you'll be scrambling for material') — both name not-knowing / not-yet-having-a-result, never wrongdoing. No shame-register language found in a full read of the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode (Big Idea / Key Concepts / WYL)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a title/bullet naming the failure ('fabrication,' 'stalling') instead of the positive discipline, making the negative case the headline. Checked every Key Concepts bullet (lines 48-51) and WYL bullet (lines 20-23): 'The audit ranked the thin spots...', 'The task went out un-packaged...', 'Traces are data. Stopping a session...is reading, not failing.', 'The run started from a pinned commit...' — all name the discipline (auditing, un-packaged send-off, reading traces, pinned-commit experiment) with failure as the addressed case, never the headline. Big Idea itself carries no failure word. Named-canonical-result carve-out not needed here (no Bainbridge-style named-practice title in this file's headings).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check — cross-module sequencing claims honoured, no front-run of downstream teaching moment
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: an early module pre-naming a later module's reveal, flattening the contrast pedagogy that reveal depends on (strategy line 398: 'the pedagogy is contrast, not prescription'). Checked every M5-facing line: prework's Willison callback (line 14) — strategy line 305 explicitly pre-clears this exact read against the M5 three-pattern reveal ('the essay never names Ronacher's three-pattern... M5's reveal is the diagnosis of the student's own M4 failures'); 'Bring to Module 5' (lines 62-66) and 'Pre-reads before Module 5' (lines 68-78, the four-piece set) match strategy line 434's approved set verbatim in shape (Uncle Bob / Entis-Klaassen / Verification asymmetry / Compound Engineering guide) and none names reference-artifact/plan.md/verifier as a named recipe. No leak found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategic themes recur in Key Concepts — ≥2-3 module-specific theme instances
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a module teaching tactics with no visible worldview underneath, so themes never compound across the training. Walked all 4 Key Concepts bullets against the doc's 6 recurring themes (lines 108-117 of strategy): bullet 1 ('the audit ranked the thin spots... filled the worst two or three') instances theme 1, 90%-correct — strategy line 108 names this exact instance ('M4's memory catches requirements-not-woven'); bullet 2 ('the task went out un-packaged... nothing but what you already had') instances theme 2, compounding — strategy line 110 names 'the memory (M4)' as a compounding-loop instance. Two clear theme-instances clears the ≥2-3 floor (floor language reads 'ge 2-3', i.e. two is sufficient). Bullets 3 and 4 are non-thematic but the rule doesn't require every bullet to carry a theme.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Key Concepts shape — breadcrumbs decorate survivors (1-3, no label/bold, 5-8 words), scored by whether a bullet lands on a compact memorable clause
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a 'Remember:'-labelled bolded tack-on that reads as trainer-bait, or a breadcrumb glued onto a bullet that should have been cut. Grepped the four Key Concepts bullets (lines 48-51) for 'Remember:' or bold wrapper — none found. Each bullet already lands as a compact, self-contained aphorism ('Traces are data. Stopping a session that has gone off the rails is reading, not failing.' reads as memorable on its own, no separate clause needed), consistent with the rule's instruction to score by whether the bullet lands memorably, not by scanning for a marker.

Grepped for mechanism-tail 'by X' constructions — none (bullet 2's 'then push back on the audit' is a second action inside the practice, not a mechanism explanation of the first).
